A.explanation: A $180^{\circ}$ phase difference is only $0.5\lambda$, but P and Q are separated by more than one full wavelength along the wave.

B.explanation: The separation is $1.25\lambda$, so phase difference is $1.25 \times 360^{\circ} = 450^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: A $540^{\circ}$ phase difference is $1.5\lambda$, which would place Q at a trough if P is at a crest, not at equilibrium.

D.explanation: A $720^{\circ}$ phase difference is $2\lambda$, which would require P and Q to be in identical states of motion two wavelengths apart.

hints: Notice the state of each point: P is at a wave crest while Q is at the equilibrium line moving downwards on the falling slope.
Recall that one full wavelength $\lambda$ corresponds to $360^{\circ}$ of phase, with crest to next crest equal to $1\lambda$ and crest to following downward zero equal to $0.25\lambda$.
Count wavelengths from the crest at P to the next identical crest, then add the extra crest-to-equilibrium fraction to reach Q before multiplying by $360^{\circ}$ per wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify the positions: P is on a crest and Q is crossing the dashed equilibrium line moving down, after one more complete crest has passed.
State the rule: phase difference $\phi = (x/\lambda) \times 360^{\circ}$, where $x$ is the distance along the direction of travel and $\lambda$ is one full cycle.
Measure $x$ in wavelengths: from the crest at P to the second crest is $1\lambda$, then from that crest down to the downward zero at Q is a further $0.25\lambda$.
Convert to phase: $\phi = 1.25 \times 360^{\circ} = 450^{\circ}$, with the same vibration direction repeated after each $360^{\circ}$ plus the extra $90^{\circ}$. This is option B.
